overview: This paper establishes a unified theoretical framework showing that diffusion model generalization arises from balanced internal representations while memorization produces spiky representations, and leverages this insight for prompt-free memorization detection and representation-space image editing.

modules.name: Synthetic Data Generation
modules.description: Generate Mixture of Gaussians (MoG) data with configurable means, covariances, and mixing weights following the paper's data distribution assumptions (Eq. 4), including support for creating separable clusters with controlled intra-cluster concentration (α) and inter-cluster separation (β) as in Definition 3.1, as well as duplicated samples for the hybrid regime (Corollary 3.4).

modules.name: Real-World Data Loading and Preprocessing
modules.description: Implement dataset loaders for CelebA, CIFAR10, ImageNet, and LAION with appropriate image transforms (normalization, resizing), support for creating small memorization subsets (e.g., 5 images for CelebA memorization) versus large generalization subsets (e.g., 10,000 images), and identification of duplicated or near-duplicated samples for hybrid regime experiments.

modules.name: Two-Layer ReLU DAE Architecture
modules.description: Implement the two-layer ReLU denoising autoencoder f(x) = W2[W1^T x]+ as defined in Eq. 5, with support for tied encoder-decoder weights (W2 = W1) and untied variants, configurable hidden dimension p for controlling over/under-parameterization regimes, and weight initialization strategies.

modules.name: Theoretical Optimal Solution Construction
modules.description: Implement the block-wise optimal solution computation from Theorem 3.1, including Gram matrix eigen-decomposition of each cluster Xk Xk^T, construction of W_Xk from top-pk eigenvectors and eigenvalues via Eq. 8, and the memorization solution (Corollary 3.2) and generalization solution (Corollary 3.3) as special cases, enabling direct comparison of learned weights with theoretical predictions.

modules.name: DAE Training Loop
modules.description: Implement the regularized DAE training objective (Eq. 6) with configurable noise level σ and weight decay λ, supporting multiple optimizers (RMSprop, Adam, AdamW), noise scheduling across multiple σ levels for full diffusion training, gradient accumulation, and logging of empirical loss convergence for both memorization and generalization regimes.

modules.name: Diffusion Sampling Pipeline
modules.description: Implement DDIM/DDPM sampling (Eq. 1) using a collection of trained DAEs across multiple noise levels with VE noise scheduling, supporting both single-step denoising evaluation and full iterative sampling to generate images from noise, with comparison between memorized DAEs (reproducing training images) and generalized DAEs (producing novel images).

modules.name: Representation Extraction and Analysis
modules.description: Extract intermediate activations h(x) = [W1^T x]+ from the ReLU DAE bottleneck, and extract features from real-world models at specified layers (EDM, DiT, SD1.4) with global max/average pooling; compute representation statistics including standard deviation, ℓ4/ℓ2 ratio, entropy, and max-min spread to quantify spikiness vs. balance.

modules.name: Memorization Detection Module
modules.description: Implement prompt-free memorization detection (Algorithm 1) using representation standard deviation as a spikiness proxy: add forward noise at timestep t, extract representation, compute STD, and classify against a threshold; support alternative metrics (ℓ4/ℓ2, entropy) and evaluation via AUROC and TPR at 1% FPR across LAION-SD1.4, ImageNet-DiT, and CIFAR10-EDM benchmarks.

modules.name: Representation Steering for Image Editing
modules.description: Implement the training-free steering method (Eq. 11) that adds a target concept's average representation vector to the source image's representation during denoising, with configurable steering strength a, support for multi-layer steering, and comparison of steering behavior between memorized (brittle, threshold-like) and generalized (smooth, progressive) samples.

modules.name: Jacobian and SVD Analysis
modules.description: Compute and analyze the denoiser Jacobian ∂f_θ/∂x for both ReLU DAEs and real-world models (SD1.4, EDM, DiT) around memorized vs. generalized samples, performing SVD to verify that memorized samples yield low-rank Jacobians dominated by the data vector while generalized samples reflect local data statistics.

modules.name: Real-World Model Integration
modules.description: Implement feature extraction hooks for pretrained diffusion models (EDM on CIFAR10, DiT-L/4 on ImageNet, Stable Diffusion v1.4 on LAION, SD3.5), with layer-specific activation capture, support for both unconditional and text-conditional generation paths, and classifier-free guidance integration for steering experiments.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics and Benchmarking
modules.description: Compute all paper evaluation metrics: AUROC and TPR at 1% FPR for memorization detection, SSCD similarity for labeling memorized vs. generalized samples, inference runtime measurement, population loss bounds for generalization error (Corollary 3.3), and KL divergence between sampled and empirical distributions for memorization quantification.

modules.name: Visualization and Plotting
modules.description: Generate all paper figures: weight matrix column visualization (Fig. 3), representation distribution histograms (Figs. 4, 5), single-sample activation bar plots, sampling result grids (Fig. 2), hybrid regime verification (Fig. 6), steering strength grids (Fig. 7), Jacobian singular value plots (Fig. 15), and eigenvalue/eigenspace alignment plots (Fig. 8).

modules.name: Experiment Configuration and Orchestration
modules.description: Manage all experimental configurations via YAML/JSON, including dataset/model/detector specifications, separability parameters (α, β), noise levels, hidden dimensions, and steering parameters; orchestrate full experimental pipelines (memorization vs. generalization training, detection benchmarking, steering evaluation, ablation studies on optimizer/noise/layers), with logging integration and reproducible checkpoint management.
